title: After the Bombs at Metal Sider, Issad Rebrab Bought One Cargo of Sugar
conflicts: The attack: 14 bombs at the Metal Sider plant (BBC Arabic) vs about 50 gunmen storming the main plant (Noonpost) vs three of his largest sites (Observ'Algérie, Afrik.com, Family Business Histories); given as differing accounts. Exile: a few months (Afrik.com, Leaders League) vs return in 1997 (Family Business Histories); story says accounts differ. Cost: only his own 1.1 billion dinar figure is used; conversions in the sources differ (>6m euros today vs ~$15.5m in 2022). Halal business: founded 1992 (Observ'Algérie) though BBC describes Paris butcher shops opened in exile; story reconciles as shops within an earlier business.
notes: Kept to the 1995 attack and the rebuilding; the 2019 detention (subject of the BBC Arabic piece) is not told. No first-person account could be read (TSA biography 404, Le Monde not loadable, issadrebrab.org down), so his claims (death threats, cost) are attributed. Two Arabic sources (BBC Arabic, Noonpost) load but the checker cannot see his Latin-script name in them. Noonpost's criticism of his political ties is noted in research_notes, not adjudicated. Quote stance: affirms.
